AS:practical_reasoning.name: Practical Reasoning

P.description: Agent who would take the action

premise_templates_en: One of the goals of {P} is {G}
Doing {A} in the situation {S1} would lead to {S2}
The goal {G} would be achieved in {S2}
AS:practical_reasoning.description_en: An agent should do an action because, in the current circumstances, it brings about a state that realizes one of the agent's goals, which promotes a value.

AS:consequences.name: Argument from Positive Consequences
AS:consequences.description_en: An action should be performed because it brings about good consequences.
AS:consequences.evidence_note_en: a source showing the action brings about the consequence

AS:values.name: Argument from Values
AS:values.conclusion_template_en: {V} is a reason to keep the goal {G}
AS:values.description_en: A value that the agent judges positive is a reason to keep a goal it favours.

AS:sign.name: Argument from Sign
AS:sign.description_en: Something is probably true because an observed sign usually indicates it.

AS:expert_opinion.name: Argument from Expert Opinion

S.example_en: human activity is warming the planet

AS:expert_opinion.description_en: A claim is plausible because an expert in its field asserts it.
AS:expert_opinion.evidence_note_en: where the expert asserts it (a citation or a link)

AS:position_to_know.name: Argument from Position to Know
premise_templates_en: {W} is in a position to know about {D}
AS:position_to_know.description_en: A claim is plausible because someone in a position to know asserts it.
AS:position_to_know.evidence_note_en: where they assert it (a citation or a link)

AS:analogy.name: Argument from Analogy
premise_templates_en: {A} is true in the case of {C}
AS:analogy.description_en: A claim holds here because it holds in a similar case.

AS:practical_reasoning_goal.name: Instrumental Practical Reasoning

P.description: Agent who would take the action

premise_templates_en: One of the goals of {P} is {G}
Doing {A} in the situation {S1} would lead to {S2}
The goal {G} would be achieved in {S2}
AS:practical_reasoning_goal.description_en: An agent should do an action because, in the current circumstances, it brings about a state in which the agent's goal is realized (goal-based, without values: Walton 2015; the book's practical inference, 22.1). For an argument that also names the value the goal promotes, use Practical Reasoning.
AS:practical_reasoning_goal.evidence_note_en: a source showing the action would bring about the state

AS:negative_consequences.name: Argument from Negative Consequences

G.example_en: higher heating bills for poor households

AS:negative_consequences.description_en: An action should not be performed because it brings about bad consequences (the counterpart of positive consequences).
AS:negative_consequences.evidence_note_en: a source showing the action brings about the consequence

AS:consequences_modal.name: Argument from Possible Positive Consequences
AS:consequences_modal.conclusion_template_en: {A} may be worth doing for the sake of {G}
AS:consequences_modal.description_en: An action may be worth doing because it may bring about a good consequence. Its conclusion bears on the decision only through the bridge from a possible good, which carries it there when the chance matters enough (D008).
AS:consequences_modal.evidence_note_en: a source showing the action could bring about the consequence

AS:negative_consequences_modal.name: Argument from Possible Negative Consequences
AS:negative_consequences_modal.conclusion_template_en: {A} may be unwise to do because of {G}
AS:negative_consequences_modal.description_en: An action may be unwise to do because it may bring about a bad consequence. Its conclusion bears on the decision only through the bridge from a possible harm, which carries it there when the chance matters enough (D008).
AS:negative_consequences_modal.evidence_note_en: a source showing the action could bring about the consequence

AS:bridge_possible_good.name: From a Possible Good Consequence to the Action (bridge)
premise_templates_en: {A} may be worth doing for the sake of {G}
The chance that doing {A} brings about {G} is large enough, given what {G} would be, to bear on whether {A} should be done
AS:bridge_possible_good.description_en: A possible good consequence counts for doing the action when its chance matters enough to the decision (D008). The move does not presume the possibility; an argument from possible positive consequences, a move of its own, supports it.

AS:bridge_possible_harm.name: From a Possible Bad Consequence to Not Acting (bridge)
premise_templates_en: {A} may be unwise to do because of {G}
The chance that doing {A} brings about {G} is large enough, given what {G} would be, to bear on whether {A} should be done
AS:bridge_possible_harm.description_en: A possible bad consequence counts against doing the action when its chance matters enough to the decision (D008). The move does not presume the possibility; an argument from possible negative consequences, a move of its own, supports it.

AS:bad_outweighs_good.name: Weighing a Bad Consequence against a Good One

H.example_en: higher heating bills for poor households

G.description: The consequence or goal it outweighs

AS:bad_outweighs_good.conclusion_template_en: Doing {A} has bad consequences that outweigh {G}
AS:bad_outweighs_good.description_en: The answer that a bad consequence of the action matters more than the good it is argued for (C003, D064, D075). It concludes the exception bad_outweighs(A,G) of the argument it answers.
AS:bad_outweighs_good.evidence_note_en: a source showing the action brings about the bad consequence

AS:good_outweighs_bad.name: Weighing a Good Consequence against a Bad One
AS:good_outweighs_bad.conclusion_template_en: Doing {A} has good consequences that outweigh {G}
AS:good_outweighs_bad.description_en: The answer that a good consequence of the action matters more than the harm it is argued against for (C003, D064, D075). It concludes the exception good_outweighs(A,G) of the argument it answers.
AS:good_outweighs_bad.evidence_note_en: a source showing the action brings about the good consequence

AS:better_means.name: Argument from a Better Means

P.description: Agent who would take the action

A2.description: Other action that would do better

premise_templates_en: One of the goals of {P} is {G}
It is possible for {P} to bring about {A2}
For {P}, {A2} would realize {G} more effectively than {A}, more surely, sooner or at lower cost
AS:better_means.conclusion_template_en: There is a way for {P} to realize the goal {G} more effectively than {A}
AS:better_means.description_en: The answer that another action open to the agent would realize the goal more effectively, more surely, sooner or at lower cost (D075, D089); an action merely as good answers nothing (D006). A move made with it records which way the other action is better.
AS:better_means.evidence_note_en: a source showing the other action would do better

AS:finding_out_first.name: Argument for Finding Out First

G.description: Possible consequence to find out about

I.example_en: a six-month trial in one office

premise_templates_en: {I} would settle, reliably enough for the decision, whether doing {A} brings about {G}
{I} can be done before the decision on {A} must be taken
The costs and risks of {I} are worth bearing to know whether doing {A} brings about {G} before that possibility counts in the decision
AS:finding_out_first.conclusion_template_en: It is worth finding out first whether doing {A} would bring about {G}, and until then that possibility should not count in deciding on {A}
AS:finding_out_first.description_en: The answer that a possible consequence should be found out before it counts in the decision, since an investigation would settle it in time, reliably enough and at a cost worth bearing (D095 (3), on the owner's declaration under D053). It defeats both bridges about the same action and consequence. A bare claim that the consequence could be found out is not this scheme, and the game refuses it at the question.
AS:finding_out_first.evidence_note_en: a source on the investigation, its timing and its cost
